# Experimental interface types
{: .no_toc}

Type-specific details of experimental interfaces: the point where hardware meets the animal or tissue, such as an implanted probe, a cranial window or an optic fiber.

## Table of contents
{: .no_toc .text-delta }

- **[Electrophysiology](#electrophysiology)**: Electrodes, arrays and pipettes that record electrical activity from neurons, nerves, muscle or heart, together with the ground and reference electrodes these recordings need.<br>[ECG](#ecg) · [ECoG](#ecog) · [EEG](#eeg) · [EMG](#emg) · [Ground electrode](#ground-electrode) · [Multi-electrode array (MEA)](#multi-electrode-array-mea) · [Nerve cuff](#nerve-cuff) · [Patch pipette](#patch-pipette) · [Reference electrode](#reference-electrode) · [Silicon probe](#silicon-probe) · [Single wire electrode](#single-wire-electrode) · [Tetrode](#tetrode) · [Tungsten microelectrode](#tungsten-microelectrode)
- **[Physiological monitoring](#physiological-monitoring)**: Sensors that monitor the subject's physiological state, such as respiration and blood pressure.<br>[Blood-pressure sensor](#blood-pressure-sensor) · [Respiratory sensor](#respiratory-sensor)
- **[Optical](#optical)**: Optical access and light-path hardware, such as cranial windows, GRIN lenses, prisms, optic fibers, objectives, miniscopes and widefield macroscopes.<br>[Cranial window](#cranial-window) · [GRIN lens](#grin-lens) · [Microscope objective](#microscope-objective) · [Miniscope](#miniscope) · [Optic fiber](#optic-fiber) · [Prism](#prism) · [Widefield macroscope](#widefield-macroscope)
- **[Assemblies](#assemblies)**: Structural hardware fixed to the skull that holds, protects or connects other interfaces, such as headposts and headcaps.<br>[Headcap](#headcap) · [Headpost](#headpost)
- **[Behavioral and Environmental](#behavioral-and-environmental)**: Sensors that observe the subject or its surroundings without contacting tissue, such as cameras, microphones and tracking systems.<br>[Camera](#camera) · [Microphone](#microphone) · [Tracking system](#tracking-system)
- **[Delivery](#delivery)**: Lines, cannulas, catheters, pumps and perfusion systems through which drugs or solutions reach the subject or tissue.<br>[Bath perfusion](#bath-perfusion) · [Catheter](#catheter) · [Drug delivery line](#drug-delivery-line) · [Injection cannula](#injection-cannula) · [Microperfusion line](#microperfusion-line) · [Osmotic pump](#osmotic-pump)
- **[Stimulation](#stimulation)**: Devices that deliver electrical, optical, magnetic, thermal or ultrasound stimulation, or present auditory, odor, tactile and visual stimuli.<br>[Auditory stimulator](#auditory-stimulator) · [LED array](#led-array) · [Olfactometer](#olfactometer) · [Stimulating electrode](#stimulating-electrode) · [TMS coil](#tms-coil) · [Tactile stimulator](#tactile-stimulator) · [Thermal probe](#thermal-probe) · [Ultrasound transducer](#ultrasound-transducer) · [Visual stimulator](#visual-stimulator)
- **[Generic](#generic)**: A fallback for interface hardware that no specific interface type covers.<br>[Generic interface](#generic-interface)
- **Other types**<br>[Target specimens](#target-specimens)

## Electrophysiology

Electrodes, arrays and pipettes that record electrical activity from neurons, nerves, muscle or heart, together with the ground and reference electrodes these recordings need.

### ECG

Electrodes recording cardiac electrical activity.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Lead configuration` | Text. The arrangement and roles of the installed ECG leads. |

### ECoG

A grid or strip array of contacts installed on the dura, on the brain surface, or on thinned skull. Created by an ECoG implant procedure; the array's design (contact count, pitch, substrate) lives on the ECoG array material row and its catalog entry.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Device identifier` | Text. The device's own identifier: the manufacturer's serial number, or the code the lab marks on the hardware and writes on the cage card and the surgery sheet. This is not the name given to this record. |
| `Placement layer` | Choice. Which tissue layer the installed array rests on: the dura, the brain surface under an opened dura, or the bone. Options: Epidural (on the dura), Subdural (on the brain surface), Epicranial (on intact or thinned skull). |
| `Reference configuration` | Text. How the array's reference input is wired as installed: a skull screw, an on-array contact or a recording contact. |

### Ground electrode

### Multi-electrode array (MEA)

A planar or grid array of electrodes, common for ex-vivo and surface recording.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Device identifier` | Text. The device's own identifier: the manufacturer's serial number, or the code the lab marks on the hardware and writes on the cage card and the surgery sheet. This is not the name given to this record. |
| `Electrode count` | Integer. The number of electrodes present on the configured array. Range: ≥ 0. |
| `Electrode pitch (µm)` | Number. Centre-to-centre distance between adjacent electrodes. Range: ≥ 0. |
| `Electrode diameter (µm)` | Number. The electrode diameter in micrometres. Range: ≥ 0. |
| `Substrate type` | Text. The material or construction type of the electrode-array substrate. |
| `Reference configuration` | Text. The reference-channel or reference-electrode arrangement used by the interface. |

### Patch pipette

A glass pipette sealed to a cell for intracellular recording.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Device identifier` | Text. The device's own identifier: the manufacturer's serial number, or the code the lab marks on the hardware and writes on the cage card and the surgery sheet. This is not the name given to this record. |
| `Patch configuration` | Choice. Patch-clamp recording configuration used. Options: Whole-cell, Cell-attached, Perforated patch, Outside-out, Inside-out, Other. |
| `Pipette resistance` | Quantity with unit. Pipette resistance in the bath before seal formation. Units: kΩ, MΩ, GΩ. |
| `Seal resistance` | Quantity with unit. Gigaseal resistance achieved before break-in (whole-cell) or during recording (cell-attached). Units: kΩ, MΩ, GΩ. |

## Other types

### Target specimens

Lists the specimens an ex-vivo interface targets, with each specimen's role relative to the interface and notes on the association.

| Field | Description |
|:------|:------------|
| `Specimen ID` | Text. The identifier of the specimen targeted by this interface entry. |
| `Role` | Text. The role of the specimen in relation to the interface. |
| `Notes` | Text (multi-line). A concise clarification specific to this target-specimen association. |

The same types are documented for API users, with property codes, versions and payload examples, on the [ExperimentalInterface schemas API page](/api/schemas/experimentalinterface/).
